prompts.prompt: Review the CDK TypeScript stack in lib/data-stack.ts before we deploy it to production. Write the findings to infra-review.md with severity, resource and line, why it matters, and a fix. Do not modify the code. No compliance framework applies beyond our general security baseline. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The obvious secrets and wildcards are easy for any reviewer; the skill's systematic per-resource checklist also catches the production-only issues (low-cardinality partition key, DESTROY removal policy, no PITR, missing DLQ/alarms, oversized Lambda) and requires a resource inventory and an explicit statement of what was not checked.

floor_checks.text: Flags the wildcard IAM statement at data-stack.ts line 45
floor_checks.check: python3 -I -c 'import re,sys;t=open("infra-review.md").read();sys.exit(0 if any(abs(int(m.group(1))-45)<=1 for m in re.finditer("(?:"+re.escape("data-stack.ts")+r"\D{0,40}?|\b[Ll]ines?\s+)(\d+)",t)) else 1)'

rubric.criterion: All four critical security issues found with lines
rubric.pass: Public bucket (publicReadAccess with only BLOCK_ACLS, L15-16), SSH 22 from 0.0.0.0/0 (L28), hardcoded DB_PASSWORD (L39), actions and resources '*' (L45-46), each rated critical
rubric.partial: Three of the four, or all four but some rated low

rubric.pass: At least three of: 'status' partition key gives a hot partition, RemovalPolicy.DESTROY on a production table, no point-in-time recovery, no DLQ/alarms/tracing/log retention on the Lambda, 3,008 MB and 15 min with no justification

Shows code-level fixes such as BlockPublicAccess.BLOCK_ALL plus enforceSSL, Secrets Manager reference, table.grantReadWriteData / bucket.grantRead instead of '*', SSM Session Manager or a known CIDR instead of 0.0.0.0/0, pointInTimeRecovery and RETAIN
rubric.partial: Fixes named in prose without code

rubric.pass: Findings grouped by severity most severe first, a resource inventory by type, and a note on limits of the review (e.g. Lambda code and synthesized template not inspected)
rubric.partial: Severity ordering present but no inventory or no limitations note

rubric.pass: Every finding maps to a real line or a real missing property; S3 encryption described accurately (not 'stored in plaintext', since S3 applies SSE-S3 by default)

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Coverage of production-only issues, not just the obvious four

prompts.prompt: Validate the CloudFormation YAML template cfn/db-template.yaml for our production environment. Write infra-review.md with each finding's severity, resource, line, impact and fix. Do not modify the template. No specific compliance standard. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill requires a resource inventory, systematic per-type checks (RDS encryption, public access, Multi-AZ, backups, deletion protection; Lambda DLQ and timeout; log retention; IAM wildcards) and CloudFormation-specific fixes such as DeletionPolicy. Without it, reviews often catch the password and public flag but skip backup, deletion policy, log retention, and right-sizing.

rubric.criterion: RDS instance issues found and rated
rubric.pass: Hardcoded MasterUserPassword (L15), StorageEncrypted false, PubliclyAccessible true as critical; BackupRetentionPeriod 0, DeletionProtection false, MultiAZ false as high or important
rubric.partial: Most of these but with some missing or misrated

rubric.pass: s3:* on Resource '*' (L36-37), Lambda with 900 s timeout and no DLQ, log group with no RetentionInDays, and an unjustified db.r6g.4xlarge

Uses template-level fixes such as ManageMasterUserPassword or a {{resolve:secretsmanager:...}} reference, DeletionPolicy/UpdateReplacePolicy Snapshot on the DB, RetentionInDays, a bucket-scoped ARN and specific actions
Has a resource inventory by type (DBInstance, Role, Function, LogGroup) and shows each was checked against the relevant categories

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Did it check every resource, not just the database?

prompts.prompt: Can you check the infrastructure code in this repo for problems? If you are missing information you need to do this well, write your questions to questions.md and stop instead of guessing.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill makes infrastructure type, path, and environment mandatory before any analysis and says not to assume what the user wants validated. Without it, a model usually reviews everything as if it were production, since the files are right there.

floor_checks.text: Stops instead of producing a full review

rubric.criterion: Asks for the environment before reviewing
rubric.pass: Asks which environment the code targets and offers the choices (development, staging, production), explaining that severity depends on it
rubric.partial: Asks about environment without choices or rationale

rubric.criterion: Uses what is discoverable and asks only what is not
rubric.pass: Notes it found a CDK TypeScript stack in lib/ and a CloudFormation template in cfn/ and asks which to validate, plus optional compliance and focus
rubric.partial: Asks for type and path without noting what it found
rubric.fail: Asks nothing about scope, or asks many questions answered by the repo

rubric.pass: No review findings written; questions are short and numbered
rubric.partial: A few preliminary findings slipped in
